title: Depth-First Search and Topological Order
summary: Going deep first - depth-first search recursively and with an explicit stack, discovery and finish order, finding cycles in directed graphs with three colours, directed acyclic graphs, topological sorting by DFS finish times and by Kahn's algorithm, using topological order for build systems, course prerequisites and longest paths, and a pointer to strongly connected components.

cards.q: In DFS cycle detection on a directed graph, which edge reveals a cycle?
cards.a:
An edge to a grey vertex, one still on the current DFS path

An edge to a finished vertex can occur without a cycle, as in a diamond shape.

cards.q: Kahn's algorithm stops with some vertices never output. What does that mean?
cards.a:
The graph has a cycle among the remaining vertices

Vertices on a cycle wait for each other, so their in-degrees never reach 0.

cards.q: Why can longest paths be found quickly in a DAG but not in general graphs?
cards.a:
In topological order, values are final before use

With no cycles, no later vertex can improve an earlier one, so one pass in topological order is enough.
